summary:
Have you always been curious about how astronauts live in space? Do you want to try the experience out yourself? Our project is the right game for you!

Our game simulates how to survive on the Moon and Mars while balancing survival needs with limited resources and power. It is designed so that young curious minds can understand and try it out too. Be careful, as every decision you make comes with a cost. Today's radiation shielding can affect tomorrow's food supply. This game acts to build awareness to the public about how astronauts deal with survival with limited power.

Think you can take on the challenge? Try the game out for yourself!
details:
1. Core Systems & Gameplay Framework

The game integrates five core operational systems to drive gameplay and learning:

  • Astronaut Movement: Directional navigation (Arrow keys / WASD) across planetary surfaces.
  • Exploration: Dynamic map transitions and backdrop switching between lunar, Martian, and base environments.
  • Survival Mechanics: Real-time tracking of life-support metrics (Oxygen, Water, Food, Energy, and Crew Health).
  • Base Building: Spending harvested minerals to construct functional infrastructure (Oxygen Generators, Water Recyclers, Greenhouses, and Solar Panels).
  • Mission Architecture: Event-driven narrative progression, NPC interactions (Scientist quests), and dynamic hazard systems.

2. Technical Implementation & Tools

  • Development Platform: Scratch
  • Key Programming Features: Use of global variables, clone objects for node harvesting, asynchronous broadcast signals for game loops, and custom operators to compute net production balancing ($Net = Production - Drain$).
  • Artificial Intelligence & Tools: Built and structured with assistance from AI generative tools to streamline narrative logic and documentation.

3. Resource Management & Economics

  • Baseline Depletion: Resources decrease after completing each task(representing one mission day), forcing players to maintain positive net production rates using constructed facilities.
  • Health & Failure States: If life-support resources drop to zero, crew health degrades progressively until a terminal failure triggers a Game Over state.
  • Victory Conditions: To complete the lunar campaign and unlock Mars, players must maintain healthy resource reserves (>50), keep crew health high, and build at least three functional facilities.
